candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — SSI surveillance
candidate.educational_objective: Apply current NHSN surveillance rules when a surgical-site infection progresses to a deeper tissue level during the surveillance period.

options.A: Keep the original superficial-incisional classification because the first classification can never be changed
options.B: Edit the event to reflect the deepest tissue level that meets SSI criteria—deep incisional in this case—and update the event date according to NHSN instructions
options.C: Automatically classify the event as organ/space because any progression beyond superficial tissue is organ/space infection
options.D: Remove the event from NHSN surveillance because an SSI that changes tissue level is no longer reportable

candidate.rationale: NHSN requires the entire SSI protocol to be followed. If a superficial-incisional SSI progresses and meets criteria at a deeper tissue level during the designated surveillance period, the event type and date are edited to reflect the deepest tissue level where SSI criteria are met. Deep-incisional and organ/space definitions are distinct; progression does not automatically make an event organ/space.
candidate.source_claim_supported: NHSN SSI classification is a surveillance/reporting framework and requires updating the event to the deepest tissue level meeting criteria during the surveillance period.
candidate.source_document_title: FAQs: Surgical Site Infections (SSI) Events; Chapter 9 Surgical Site Infection Event
candidate.source_locator: SSI FAQ Q25–Q26; Chapter 9 January 2026: when superficial SSI progresses deeper within surveillance period, edit event type/date to deepest tissue level meeting criteria
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — NHSN
candidate.stem: During NHSN surgical-site-infection surveillance, an infection initially met superficial-incisional SSI criteria. Later, within the designated surveillance period, the same event meets deep-incisional SSI criteria. How should the infection-prevention nurse report the event?
